title: Lloyd Arthur Andres (1928-2024)
content: Lloyd Andres was born on 17 May 1928 in Santa Ana in Orange County, California. He was raised on an orange ranch in Anaheim, also in Orange County, where Disneyland is located. During his high school years, he did part-time work picking oranges and helping his father treat orchards for pest control. Lloyd received his B.S. in Entomology from UCLA in 1950. He earned his master's degree in entomology at the University of California- Berkeley in 1952 for his study of encyrtid parasitoids of a mealybug. His Ph.D. degree in entomology was awarded in 1957, also at UC-Berkeley, where he studied the ecology of spider mites (Tetranychus spp.) for his dissertation. Lloyd was an assistant entomologist at the University of California Citrus Research Station in Riverside, California, from 1956 until 1958. He then began his 31-year career with the United States Department of Agriculture- Agricultural Research Service (USDA-ARS) as a research entomologist, research leader, and national investigations leader.
